add.err.ErrInvalidSignature: This bundle's signature doesn't match its publisher key. The file is corrupt, was tampered with, or was signed by a different publisher than expected.
add.err.ErrFingerprintMismatch: The publisher key inside the bundle doesn't match the fingerprint the manifest claims. Re-export the bundle from the publisher.
add.err.ErrMissingManifest: This bundle is missing its manifest. It may be incomplete — re-export from the publisher.
add.err.ErrMissingSignature: This bundle is missing its signature. It may be incomplete — re-export from the publisher.
add.err.ErrMissingPublisherKey: This bundle is missing the publisher's public key. Re-export from the publisher.
add.err.ErrInvalidPublisherKey: The publisher public key in this bundle is malformed.
add.err.ErrUnsupportedSpec: This bundle uses a spec version this app doesn't understand yet. Update Daal.
add.err.ErrExpiredBundle: This bundle has expired. Ask the publisher for a fresh one.
add.err.ErrExpiredRoute: One or more routes inside this bundle have expired.
add.err.ErrMissingProfile: A route in this bundle is missing its profile data.
add.err.ErrUnsafePath: This bundle contains an unsafe archive path and was rejected.
add.err.ErrInvalidEnum: This bundle contains a route with an unknown scarcity class or transport family.
add.err.ErrRevokedRoute: One or more routes in this bundle have been revoked.
add.err.ErrJson: This bundle's manifest could not be parsed.
add.err.ErrZip: This file is not a valid Daal bundle (zip parse failed).
add.err.ErrHex: A field in this bundle is not valid hex.
add.err.ErrTime: A date/time field in this bundle is malformed.
add.err.identity_missing: You haven't created a Daal address on this phone yet. Tap My address to create one, then ask the publisher to re-issue the .sbpx for your new address.
add.err.custody_locked: Device custody is locked. Unlock with your session passphrase, then try again.
add.err.not_envelope: This file isn't a sealed .sbpx envelope. If it's a plain .sbp bundle, you don't need a PIN.
add.err.envelope_corrupt: This .sbpx couldn't be opened. It may be sealed for a different address, the PIN may be wrong, or the file may be corrupt.

settings.custody.rotated_toast: Identity rotated. Your new address is shown above.
settings.custody.lock_now.help: Drops the in-memory wrap key. You'll be asked for your session passphrase next time.
settings.custody.rotate.help: Mint a new Daal address. Old packs still open because the previous key is kept in history.
settings.custody.rotate.dialog.title: Rotate your Daal address?
settings.custody.rotate.dialog.body: This mints a fresh keypair and a new daal1… address. Your previous key is kept under a versioned alias so already-sealed .sbpx packs still open. Tell your publishers about the new address so future packs reach you.
settings.custody.rotate.dialog.checkbox: I understand publishers must learn my new address.
subs.empty.title: No subscriptions yet
subs.empty.help: Paste a subscription URL on the Network page to add one. They refresh on their own.
subs.confirm_remove.title: Remove this subscription?
subs.confirm_remove.help: Routes already imported from it will stay. Future refreshes stop.
pub.recipients.title: Recipients
pub.recipients.empty.title: No recipients yet
pub.recipients.empty.help: Add a friend's daal1… address to start distributing routes.
pub.recipients.revoke.title: Revoke recipient?
pub.recipients.revoke.body: Revoke {name}? They lose access on the next freshness rotation.
pub.recipients.remove.title: Remove from list?
pub.recipients.remove.body: Remove {name} from your roster for good? This only clears the local record — it was already revoked on the server.
pub.recipients.rotate.title: Give {name} a new key?
pub.recipients.rotate.body: The relay will issue {name} a fresh key and cancel the one they have now. The file they are using stops working the moment this finishes, so you will have to send them the new one. Nobody else needs a new file — everyone else keeps connecting with the one they already have, though every connection on this relay briefly drops and comes back.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.title: {name} has a new key
pub.recipients.rotate.done.body: The old key is cancelled. Until {name} imports the new file they cannot connect, and Daal has no way to send it to them over the network — hand it to them yourself. Everyone else on this relay was left alone.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.box_keys: The relay did more than it was asked: it replaced its own identity as well, so EVERY file you have handed out has stopped working — not only {name}'s. Rebuild each one in the files list above and deliver them all again.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.unverified: The relay would not say which parts of itself it rewrote, so nothing confirmed the old key is gone everywhere. Treat the old file as possibly still working until this relay's management service is updated.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.nofile: The key was changed on the relay, but the new file could not be built. {name} is disconnected until you rebuild it — use Rebuild in the files list above.
pub.recipients.add.title: Add recipient
pub.recipients.add.bad_address: That doesn't look like a daal1… address.
pub.relays.title: Relays
pub.relays.destroy.title: Remove {name}?
pub.relays.destroy.intro: Two very different things go by that word. Pick the one you mean.
pub.relays.destroy.local.title: Remove from Daal only
pub.relays.destroy.local.body: Erases this relay’s signing key and cloud token from this app and drops it from your list. The server itself keeps running and keeps billing, and connection files you have already handed out keep working. Write the address down now — afterwards Daal can no longer show it to you, and your provider’s console is the only place left to delete it.
pub.relays.destroy.address.unknown: Daal has no address for this server.
pub.relays.destroy.server.title: Delete the server too
pub.relays.destroy.server.body: Destroys the cloud server itself, along with the SSH key and firewall Daal created for it. Everyone using this relay loses their connection the moment it goes, billing stops, and none of it can be undone or recovered.
pub.relays.destroy.server.noaddr: Daal never recorded an address for this relay, so it will look the server up by the name it gave it. If it cannot find it, the report will say so and you will have to finish the job in your provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.error.local: Nothing was removed. The relay is still in Daal — try again.
pub.relays.destroy.error.server: The server was NOT deleted, and nothing was removed from Daal. It is still running and still billing — try again, or delete it yourself in your cloud provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.report.title: What happened
pub.relays.destroy.report.ok: The server is gone and the billing has stopped. Anyone who was using this relay is disconnected now.
pub.relays.destroy.report.local_only: Removed from Daal. The server is still running and still billing — delete it in your cloud provider’s console to stop the charges.
pub.relays.destroy.report.server_failed: The server was NOT deleted. It is still running and still billing, and Daal can no longer reach it — delete it yourself in your cloud provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.report.leftovers: The server is gone, but Daal could not clear everything it had created alongside it. The leftovers cost nothing, but they can block a new relay in the same region — remove them in your provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.report.local_kept: The relay is still in Daal. Nothing on this device was erased, so you can try again once the problem above is sorted out.
pub.relays.status.disclaimer: Setup state — not a live health check.
pub.relays.empty.title: No relays yet
pub.relays.empty.body: A relay is your own small server. You create one, then hand out a connection file to the people you want to share it with.
pub.artifacts.title: Files to share
pub.artifacts.shared.title: Everyone pack (.sbp)
pub.artifacts.shared.missing.title: No everyone pack yet
pub.artifacts.shared.missing.body: This is the one file anyone in your family can import on any phone. Build it once and share it as often as you like.
pub.artifacts.rotate.title: Rotate the everyone pack?
pub.artifacts.rotate.body: This mints new shared credentials. Every copy of the pack you have already handed out will stop working and everyone will need the new file. Use it if the old one leaked; use plain Share otherwise.
pub.artifacts.raw.title: Raw signed bundle (.sbp)
pub.artifacts.sbpx.missing: This recipient's file was never written. Rebuild it to try again.
pub.recipients.adding_detail: Opening a 5-minute window on the server firewall, minting credentials, and registering the recipient. Stay on this screen — typically 10–30 seconds.
pub.recipients.err_unreachable: The server isn't answering on its management port. If it was created with an older build of Daal it can't be patched in place — remove it from Daal in the danger zone below, delete the server in your provider's console, and deploy a fresh one.
pub.helper_ip.title: Your network address changed
pub.helper_ip.body: Daal opens a short-lived opening in the server's firewall for the address you're connecting from. We couldn't work it out automatically — check the address below and try again.
pub.helper_ip.stale: Couldn't reach the relay from this network.
pub.danger.title: Danger zone
pub.danger.recovery.title: Save a recovery key
pub.danger.recovery.body: This relay's signing key lives on this device only. If you lose the device you can never add or remove anyone again. Save a copy somewhere safe — but read the warning first: the file is NOT encrypted.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.title: Change this relay's disguise
pub.danger.rotate_tls.body: The relay disguises itself as an ordinary web server at one hostname. If that hostname has been singled out and blocked, changing it can bring the relay back — at the cost of every connection file you have handed out.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.title: Change the disguise on {relay}?
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.body: Every connection file you have handed out stops working the moment this finishes — the everyone pack and each person's own file alike. Daal cannot send new settings over the network yet, so nothing repairs itself: you have to rebuild each file on this screen and deliver it by hand, one person at a time. Nobody's key changes and the relay keeps running; only the disguise moves.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.count: {count} people are holding a file that will stop working.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.count_none: Nobody is holding a file from this relay yet, so right now this costs you nothing.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.count: {count} people are holding a file that has stopped working.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.count_none: Nobody was holding a file from this relay, so this cost you nothing.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.title: Disguise changed
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.next: Every file you have handed out is dead. Rebuild the everyone pack and each person's file in the list above, then deliver each one by hand — there is still no way to push them over the network.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.unknown: The relay would not confirm which hostname it landed on, so the name above is the one that was asked for, not one that was checked. The files Daal builds will use it — if people still cannot connect after importing them, this relay's management service needs updating.
pub.rotate.too_old: This relay's management service is older than this app and cannot do that on its own, so nothing was changed. That service is fixed when the relay is created and cannot be patched in place — it needs a new release of Daal, or a fresh relay.
pub.danger.decommission.title: Remove this relay
pub.danger.decommission.body: Take it out of Daal and leave the server running, or delete the server as well and stop the billing. You pick which on the next screen.
pub.custody.label.hardware: Protected by this device's secure hardware. The key cannot be copied off this device.
pub.custody.label.os_keystore: Protected by this device's system keystore — software only, with no dedicated secure hardware.
pub.custody.label.session_passphrase: Protected by a session passphrase you type once each time Daal starts. This device has no keystore Daal can use, so the protection is only as strong as your passphrase.
pub.custody.broken.title: Can't reach this device's key store
pub.custody.broken.body: Daal can't open the place where this relay's signing key is kept, so every publisher action would fail halfway. Nothing has been lost. Restart the app; if it keeps happening, export a recovery key while you still can.
pub.custody.recovery.help: Export a recovery key while one is still readable:
pub.custody.migrate.title: One-time security upgrade
pub.custody.migrate.body: Daal no longer uses a PIN. Your relay's keys move into this device's own protected storage and you'll never be asked for the PIN again. Enter it once to complete the move.
pub.custody.migrate.warn: Don't skip this. If you do, the signing key for {n} relay(s) becomes permanently unreadable — you could never add or remove anyone on them again.
pub.custody.migrate.done: Done. Your keys are protected by this device now, and the PIN is gone for good.
pub.custody.migrate.partial: Some items couldn't be moved. Your old copies are untouched — nothing has been lost.
pub.custody.unlock.title: Unlock your publisher keys
pub.custody.unlock.body: This device has no keystore Daal can use, so your keys are protected by a session passphrase. Enter it once per launch.
pub.danger.recovery.confirm:
Save an unencrypted recovery key?

The file contains this relay’s signing key in the clear. It goes to your Downloads folder, where any app with storage access can read it, and Daal’s emergency wipe cannot remove it. Anyone who gets this file can impersonate your relay.

Move it to secure storage and delete it from Downloads as soon as you have.
pub.custody.recovery.confirm:
Save an unencrypted recovery key?

The file contains this relay’s signing key in the clear. It goes to your Downloads folder, where any app with storage access can read it, and Daal’s emergency wipe cannot remove it. Anyone who gets this file can impersonate your relay.

Move it to secure storage and delete it from Downloads as soon as you have.
pub.artifacts.sbpx.revoked: Revoked. Their file no longer works and cannot be rebuilt — add them again if you want to give them access.
pub.artifacts.shared.build.title: Build the everyone pack?
pub.artifacts.shared.build.body: Building mints fresh shared credentials on the relay. If you have already handed out an everyone pack for this relay — even though the file is missing from this device — those copies will stop working and everyone will need the new file.
pub.custody.unlock.create.title: Choose a passphrase
pub.custody.unlock.create.body: This device has no keystore Daal can use, so your publisher keys are protected by a passphrase you choose now and type once each time Daal starts. It is never stored and cannot be recovered — if you forget it, the relay’s signing key is gone and you could never add or remove anyone on it again. Type it twice.
pub.custody.unlock.create.mismatch: Those don't match. Type the same passphrase twice.
pub.custody.unlock.regression: If you have never set a passphrase on this device, nothing is lost: your system keystore has stopped answering. Unlock your login keyring (or restart the device) and reopen Daal.
pub.custody.migrate.stuck.body: The PIN was never stored anywhere, so there is no way to recover it and no way to read the old key without it. The only way forward is to remove the affected relay from Daal and start a new one. Its server keeps running and billing until you delete it in your provider’s console.
pub.custody.migrate.stuck.confirm:
Remove {name} from Daal?

Its signing key is unreadable without the PIN, so this is permanent: you will never be able to add or remove anyone on that relay again. The server at {ip} keeps running and keeps billing — delete it in your cloud provider’s console.
